new_task_1.title: Set standard CMake try-compile configuration from Conan build_type
new_task_1.description: Conan 2.18.0 updates `CMakeToolchain` so generated toolchains predefine `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION` for the standard CMake build types. This makes CMake `try_compile()` and related checks use the active Conan configuration during cross builds while leaving custom configurations unset and still allowing an explicit user override.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated CMake toolchains propagate Conan's standard `settings.build_type` into `try_compile()` checks so configuration-specific compiler tests run with the intended build type, without forcing custom configuration names or overriding a user-supplied value.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeToolchain` renders its try-compile block and `settings.build_type` is one of `Debug`, `Release`, `RelWithDebInfo`, or `MinSizeRel`, the generated `conan_toolchain.cmake` should emit a guarded `set(CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION <build_type>)` before the `IN_TRY_COMPILE` check. If the build type is missing or is a custom configuration name, the generated toolchain should omit this setting. The generated block must keep the `if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION)` guard so a user-provided value is not overwritten.
expectation.conceptual: Cross-build compiler checks should run under the same standard configuration Conan is generating for. Conan should help CMake choose the right standard config automatically, but it should not guess custom config names or block users from supplying their own try-compile configuration.

constraints.grounded: Only the four standard CMake configurations are eligible for automatic emission. Do not emit `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION` for custom build types, and do not set it unconditionally when the variable is already defined by the user or command line. Existing try-compile short-circuit behavior through the `IN_TRY_COMPILE` property must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This should be a narrow compatibility fix for standard CMake configurations. It must not turn Conan into a generic custom-config mapper or override a caller that already knows which try-compile configuration it wants.

behavior: Generated `conan_toolchain.cmake` files now set `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION` for standard Conan build types before handling `IN_TRY_COMPILE`.
The generated assignment is wrapped in `if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION)` so user-provided values still win.
Automatic try-compile configuration is limited to `Debug`, `Release`, `RelWithDebInfo`, and `MinSizeRel`.
Custom or unknown build-type names do not cause Conan to emit `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION`.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan generates a CMake toolchain for a cross build with `settings.build_type=Release`, the resulting `conan_toolchain.cmake` should contain `set(CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION Release)` inside the guarded try-compile block.
When Conan generates a CMake toolchain for another standard configuration such as `Debug`, the resulting toolchain should emit that standard configuration as the try-compile configuration.
When Conan generates a CMake toolchain for a custom build type, the resulting toolchain should not define `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION` automatically.
When a user defines `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION` externally, the Conan-generated block should not overwrite that value.

new_task_2.title: Gate editable generator rewriting behind `--build=editable`
new_task_2.description: Conan 2.18.0 changes editable package installation so generator files are only rewritten, and editable `build()` is only run, when the editable node is actually selected for build. Ordinary installs of consumers that depend on editables no longer refresh the editable package's generated files unless `--build=editable` makes that dependency a `BINARY_EDITABLE_BUILD`.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that editable dependencies do not rewrite their generator output as an install side effect unless the caller explicitly requests editable builds, while preserving the existing generator rewrite and build execution for editables that are selected for build.

expectation.grounded: During editable package installation, Conan must still resolve the editable's base folders, but it should only log `Rewriting files of editable package ...`, call `write_generators()`, and invoke `run_build_method()` when `node.binary == BINARY_EDITABLE_BUILD`. If the editable dependency is present in the graph but is not marked for editable build, Conan should skip those rewrite/build side effects.
expectation.conceptual: Editable packages should behave like opt-in build participants, not as dependencies whose generator state is always rewritten during every consumer install. Users who want Conan to refresh editable outputs should request editable builds explicitly.

constraints.grounded: Do not stop Conan from setting editable base folders before later processing. Do not change the explicit editable-build path: when an editable node is classified as `BINARY_EDITABLE_BUILD`, Conan must still rewrite generator files and run the editable build flow. Limit the behavior change to suppressing rewrite/build side effects for non-build editable nodes.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should reduce unintended install-time side effects without breaking the explicit editable build workflow. It should not alter unrelated editable metadata resolution or package-folder layout handling.

behavior: Editable package generator rewriting now happens only when the editable node is in `BINARY_EDITABLE_BUILD` state.
Editable package `build()` execution remains tied to `BINARY_EDITABLE_BUILD` and continues to run only in that explicit build mode.
Installs that include editable dependencies but do not request editable builds no longer emit the editable rewrite message or regenerate those editable generator files.
Workflows that need editable generator output during install must opt in with `--build=editable`.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer install traverses an editable dependency without `--build=editable`, Conan should not rewrite files in that editable package's generators folder as part of the install.
When the same install is run with `--build=editable` so the editable becomes `BINARY_EDITABLE_BUILD`, Conan should rewrite the editable package's generator files and run its build flow.
When editable layouts depend on generated build-folder content, those files should still be produced when the install explicitly includes `--build=editable`.
When Conan processes a non-build editable dependency, it should still resolve the editable's base folders without performing the generator rewrite/build side effects.

new_task_3.title: Restore argument parsing for simple info and listing commands
new_task_3.description: Conan 2.18.0 makes several commands that previously bypassed argument parsing participate in the normal CLI parser flow: `conan version`, `conan profile list`, `conan editable list`, and `conan remote list-users`. This restores consistent handling for help and other parser-managed options on commands that otherwise just returned data directly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that simple commands with no command-specific arguments still invoke the normal Conan argument parser so standard help and parser-managed options are handled consistently instead of being skipped.

expectation.grounded: Before executing their underlying API calls, the `version`, `profile list`, `editable list`, and `remote list-users` command handlers should call `parser.parse_args(*args)`. Invocations that use parser-managed options such as `-h` should therefore enter the normal parsing/help path instead of bypassing parsing entirely, while plain invocations without extra arguments should continue returning the same command data.
expectation.conceptual: Commands should not behave differently just because they happen to accept no custom arguments. Users should get the same parser behavior, help handling, and argument validation across the CLI surface.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the default result payloads for `conan version`, `conan profile list`, `conan editable list`, or `conan remote list-users` when they are invoked without extra arguments. Limit the change to making those handlers enter the standard parser flow before performing their work.
constraints.conceptual: This is a consistency fix, not a redesign of those commands. The commands should keep their existing purpose and output, but stop silently skipping parser behavior.

behavior: `conan version` now invokes the standard parser before returning version information.
`conan profile list` and `conan editable list` now invoke the standard parser before listing cached profiles or editables.
`conan remote list-users` now invokes the standard parser before listing logged-in remote users.
Parser-managed options such as help are now handled through the usual command parsing path for these commands.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan version -h` is invoked, the command should enter the normal parser help flow instead of bypassing argument parsing and executing directly.
When `conan profile list -h`, `conan editable list -h`, or `conan remote list-users -h` is invoked, each command should likewise go through normal parser handling.
When these commands are invoked without extra arguments, they should continue to return their existing version or listing results.
When unsupported extra arguments are passed to one of these commands, the normal parser validation path should run instead of silently ignoring those arguments.
